Origin & botanical facts
The name orange, “naranga” in Sanskrit,
comes from the Tamil “naru” and means
good guide to quality because some
oranges are artificially colored to preserve
shelf life and to enhance appeal and
marketability.  
The fruit is a great snack, although
most Americans consume oranges in the
form of juice.  Oranges are a versatile
cooking ingredient.  The skin is used
commercially in candy and is the base for
various liqueurs and cordials.
Nutrient composition
Oranges are high in vitamin C and are a
good source of folate.  Oranges (but not
their juice) are good sources of fiber.  Both
contain antioxidants that promote health.
